records.label: spacr.qt.resonance.settle#2
records.source: ``tightness`` below 1 leaves the particles short of the lines, which is what a plate driven gently looks like: the sand gathers but does not resolve. It is the control that makes silence read as a loose cloud and a loud passage as a figure. It may be one number for every particle or ONE PER PARTICLE, and per particle is what the backdrop uses: a plate where every grain converges equally draws a wire diagram, and a real one has a haze of sand that never quite arrives. The haze is what makes the picture look like sand rather than like a plot of an equation.

records.source: A SUGGESTION IS JUDGED, NOT RELABELLED (item 512). A crop Suggest proposed a class for wears an amber ``?`` badge beside its dashed ring. A click or ``Y`` confirms it (it becomes an ordinary label and wears a green tick); a right-click or ``N`` rejects it (it goes back to unanswered and wears a red cross); ``U`` undoes either. records.label: spacr.qt.screens.embeddings#4
records.source: **What it needs.** Crops, and a choice about the channels. The crops come from the row at the top of the screen, which is :mod:`spacr.crop_loader`: either a ``measurements.db``, narrowed to one object class, one plate or any condition its crop table supports, or a folder of crop PNGs. Whichever it is, the pixels are read the way every other screen reads them -- :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source` decides between the crops already under ``data/`` and cutting them from ``merged/*.npy``, and says which it chose. Nothing has to be prepared first: a plate that has been through Measure with crop output on is ready.
records.context: **What it needs.** Extracted image regions, and a choice about the channels. The extracted image regions come from the row at the top of the application view, which is :mod:`spacr.crop_loader`: either a ``measurements.db``, narrowed to one object class, one laboratory microplate or any condition its extracted-image-region table supports, or a folder of extracted image region PNGs. Whichever it is, the pixels are read the way every other application view reads them -- :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source` decides between the extracted image regions already under ``data/`` and cutting them from ``merged/*.npy``, and says which it chose. Nothing has to be prepared first: a laboratory microplate that has been through Measure with extracted image region output on is ready.
records.translation: **Hvað það þarf.** Myndskurði, og val um rásirnar. Hvort heldur sem er eru pixlarnir lesnir eins og hver önnur skjámynd les þá -- :func:`spacr.crops.resolve_crop_source` velur á milli myndskurðanna sem þegar eru undir ``data/`` og þess að skera þá úr ``merged/*.npy``, og segir hvort það valdi.
